questions.q: Erroneous examples are injected into the training dataset. Which threat is this?
questions.explain: Poisoning targets the training data upstream of the model.

questions.q: An analyzed document contains 'ignore system instructions.' Which threat is this?
questions.explain: A hostile instruction embedded in processed content hijacks the prompt: prompt injection.

questions.q: The model provides a convincing but completely fabricated answer. Which concept is this?
questions.explain: A hallucination is a false output presented with confidence.

questions.q: Which concepts relate to privacy and data protection? (Select all that apply)
questions.explain: Data loss and privacy relate to confidentiality. Bias and explainability relate to model quality and governance.

questions.q: An AI agent has shell access and executes an unauthorized command. Which concept is this?
questions.explain: A tool-enabled agent can be tricked into executing code: this is the 'Code execution' threat.

questions.q: Why is this chapter marked 'beyond the textbooks'?
options: The textbooks treat AI as a defensive tool only
questions.explain: The four textbooks mention ML/AI for detection (EDR, UEBA) but never as a threat vector: this content comes from official objective 2.6.
